PART V DAMP HEAT (CYCLIC) TEST

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part V ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 August 1982, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council.

0.2 Fast development in the field of instruments has brought ? significant change in their basic content and design. It has been felt over the year that IS: 2352-1963* does not cater for the present day needs of the instruments and is also not in line with the recent trends in climatic and environmental testing procedures to be adopted for improving their quality and reliability. It has, therefore, become necessary to have uniform and more rational testing procedures as far as possible. This series of standards on climatic and durability tests ( IS : 10236) has been prepared with this objective. 0.2.1 It is proposed to withdraw the existing Indian Standard ( IS : 23521963 )* as soon as the tests mentioned therein are covered in the new series ( IS: 10236).

5. TEST CHAMBER 5.1 The chamber

4.1 The instrument

used for this test shall meet the requirements

given

in 5.1.1 to 5.1.9. 5.1.1 The chamber shall be capable of controlling and varying the temperature of the working space cyclically between 20f5"C and 40+2"C.
NOTE - The test chamber temperature conditions. may require a cooling unit to meet the above

5.1.2 The chamber shall be capable of achieving in its working space, the rate of change of temperature as required in 7.3 and 7.5. 5.1.3 The chamber shall be capable of maintaining relative humidity of not less then 95 percent at all temperatures of the cycle. 5.1.4 The temperature and humidity of the chamber shall be monitored by sensing devices suitably located in the working space. 5.1.5 The air in the chamber shall be continuously agitated to ensure that the conditions throughout the chamber are homogeneous and are as near as possible to those prevailing in the immediate vicinity of the sensing device. 5.1.6 Care shall be taken that specimen under test is not subjected to direct radiations from the heating element of the chamber, 5.1.7 Condensed water shall be continuously drained from the chamber and shall not be used again until it has been purified. 5.1.8 Water used for maintenance of chamber resistivity of not less than 500 ohm metre. humidity shall have a

5.1.9 Condensed water from the walls and the roof of the chamber shall not fall on the specimen. 4

IS : 10236 ( Part V ) - 1982 6. TEST SEVERITIES 6.1 The test severity indicated by number of cycles of temperature changes shall be as specified in the relevant instrument specification. It may be selected from the following: 7 14 28 56 84 cycles cycles cycles cycles cycles 1 :
I

Each cycle ( 24 hours ) of temperature from 20�C to 40�C and back to 20�C with relative humidity of not less than 9.5 percent.

J

7. TEST PROCEDURE 7.1 The instrument condition. shall be subjected to this test in the unpacked

7.2 At the laboratory temperature the instrument under test shall be introduced into the chamber whose temperature is maintained at 20&5"C. 7.3 The temperature and relative humidity of the chamber shall then be raised to 40&2"C and 95 percent ( minimum ) respectively over a period of 3 hours. 7.4 The above conditions shall be maintained for a period of 12 hours. 7.5 The temperature of the chamber shall then be lowered to 2Of5"C over a period of 3 hours. Saturation of the chamber atmosphere with water vapour shall occur during this period but water shall not drip on the instrument from the roof of the chamber. 7.6 The temperature of the chamber shall be further maintained at 20+5"C for the remaining period to complete the duration of 24 hours from the start. 7.7 The procedure given in 7.2 to 7.6 constitutes one cycle. 7.8 The instrument shall be subjected to 7, 14, 28, 56 or 84 such cycles as required by the relevant instrument specification. Number of cycles shall be decided on the basis of conditions of use and storage and degree of protection envisaged for the store. 7.9 At the completion of every seven cycles the instrument shall be visually examined and performance check of electrical/electronic arrangement, if fitted in it, shall be carried out as required by the relevant instrument specification. 7.10 Recovery - After specified number of cycles the instrument shall be finally taken out of the chamber. Any condensed water adhering to the instrument shall be removed by shaking. The instrument shall then be kept under standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two hours. 5

IS : 10236 ( Part V ) - 1982 8. FINAL MEASUREMENTS 8.1 After recovery the instrument shall be visually examined and tested for its performance in accordance with the relevant instrument specification.

9. DETAILS TO BE GIVEN IN RELEVANT INSTRUMENT
SPECIFICATION 9.1 When this test is included in the ielevant instrument specification, the following details shall be given as far as applicable for carrying out this test:

a) Initial observations/measurements; b) Number of cycles; c) Visual examination and performance check, if necessary, to be carried out during conditioning after completion of every seven cycles; d) Duration of recovery if other than specified; e) Final observations/measurements; and f) Any deviation from the normal procedure.
